title: White Rice with Carrots and Dark Green Vegetables

content.title: About
content.content: This dish consists of boiled white rice, fresh carrots, and dark green vegetables (such as broccoli, spinach or green beans). It is rich in carbohydrates, B‑vitamins, vitamin A from carrots, and vitamins C and K from the green vegetables.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: White rice is a staple food in many Asian countries.
Carrots contain beta‑carotene, which the body converts into vitamin A.
Dark green vegetables are among the richest sources of vitamin K and folate.
Combining rice with vegetables creates a more nutritionally balanced meal.
Traditionally these combinations are steamed or cooked in a pot without added fat.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Rice provides a quick source of energy thanks to easily digestible carbohydrates.

items.title: Eye health
items.content: Beta‑carotene from carrots supports healthy vision.

items.title: Bone health
items.content: Vitamin K from dark green vegetables contributes to bone mineralization.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamin C from the green vegetables boosts the immune system.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The dish is prepared without added oil, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: White rice can raise blood sugar quickly, so people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Vegetable allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to certain green vegetables.

items.title: Food contaminants
items.content: Insufficiently washed vegetables may retain pesticide residues; thorough rinsing is recommended before cooking.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish as a side to meat, fish, or tofu, or enjoy it as a light main course. Cook the rice until tender, dice the carrots and lightly steam them, and blanch or steam the green vegetables to retain color and nutrients.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. When reheating, add a splash of water to prevent drying out.
